text:
oliver: Heads up — we've got a burst of NVMe write errors in ap-southeast1 starting ~03:12 UTC. GPU provisioning queues started piling up, saw ~120 pending attaches. Attaching logs now.

maria: Can you paste smartctl output + janitor logs?

oliver: ```
# smartctl -a /dev/nvme0n1
Media_Error_Count: 3
Reallocated_Sector_Ct: 14 -> 18
Vendor-specific: esd_event_count=4, last_esd_ts=2026-03-22T03:14Z
```

infra-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: nvme_error_rate (ap-southeast1) = 0.67% (threshold 0.5%) — triggered 03:18 UTC

kevin: Are these concentrated on a single cohort or spread across racks/hosts? correlated with last night's janitor run?

tara: Janitor ran a deep-scrub between 02:50–03:30. Concurrency was bumped to 12 for the maintenance window to clear backlog. We overlapped with a vendor rack re-cabling at ~03:05.

oliver: I suspect ESD/transient hardware after the re-cabling — error bursts look electrostatic (vendor flag in SMART). I disabled janitor on the most-affected pool (pool-az3-hot) to stop write churn. That dropped immediate attach retries but backlog remains.

maria: Short-term mitigation: patch janitor config -> set cleaner.max_concurrency=4 and enable cleaner.write_coalesce=true. That should reduce small write amplification + in-flight write stalls. I'll push to a 1/50 canary.

kevin: If coalescing reduces write IOPS, we should also allow read-only attaches for downtime-tolerant GPU jobs so provisioning can continue while we triage. Rollout plan?

infra-bot: Deploy started: cleaner-config patch (canary 1/50) by maria — https://deploys.internal/cleaner/patch/8331

maria: Canary report after 18m: no new esd events on canary hosts, attach success rate up from 68% -> 96% :thumbsup: CPU usage on janitor lower, iops down ~42%.

tara: Follow-up: open a hardware ticket with the colo vendor. Pattern + timing matches possible improper grounding after the re-cabling work. I'll cc ops and site.

oliver: PV-4829 opened with vendor (site visit scheduled tomorrow). Also preparing rollback/runbook if errors spike on rollout.

kevin: Cost impact note: provisioning delays added ~2.3 GPU-hours during the spike and ~1200 USD/day in marginal on-demand fallback for queued jobs. Please tag PV-4829 for finance review.

oliver: Thanks. I'll keep monitoring dashboards and post a short postmortem draft after vendor visit. Dropping key snippets below for the incident log.

---
# key snippets
- janitor job: cleaner/2026-03-22T02:49Z id=cleaner-8842 (concurrency=12)
- affected pool: pool-az3-hot (hosts: az3-nvme-0[12-23])
- sample SMARTs: esd_event_count incrementing, media_err spikes at 03:08–03:16
- mitigation executed: cleaner.max_concurrency=4, cleaner.write_coalesce=true (canary 1/50)
- vendor ticket: PV-4829 (site visit booked)

maria: I'll keep the canary running and ramp if stable. If anyone sees new attach failures please ping me directly.

kevin: Adding a finance/ops follow-up item.

tara: Great triage team. We'll include grounding checklist in the postmortem. :eyes:
